Posted November 20, 2007 

Analysis by Richard Cowan  

(MarijuanaNews note: I think that is an excellent practice to have Guest Opinions on newspaper editorial pages especially from public officials who want to explain their position on current issues.  

 

But what is the moral/professional obligation of the editors and publishers when the official then abuses that forum to lie badly and blatantly to the papers readers?  

 

Recently, I analyzed an example of this problem that appeared in the New York Times. 

See
Oh, Joy! New Lies From the Czars Little Helper, In The New York Times, Appropriately.
  

Over the last decade, I have examined other instances, some worse than others. 

For example: The Los Angeles Times Once Again Gives Space for McCaffrey And An Aide To Lie To Its Readers.
and 

The Heritage Foundation Uses The Florida Drug Czar To Lie To Conservatives About Medical Marijuana. Very Badly. 
 

If the politician does not have a track record, or if he says something new, then the editors might be forgiven for failing to uphold basic standards. But if the politician has a long record of deceit and the lies are basic parts of what should be a well-known party line then the editors have failed their readers if they do not report that the public official is a liar.

 

In this case, Florida Attorney General Bill McCollum formerly a member of the US House of Representatives has a very long record and is a very incompetent liar. That is, he lies badly, and his obvious dishonesty should disqualify him from holding any public office.  

 

McCollums record: 

When McCollum was in the House he was one of the most extreme opponents of medical marijuana. Ironically, his accomplice in much of this malfeasance was Bob Barr (R-GA) who has left the Congress and has lobbied FOR medical marijuana. 

 

Here is an article from MarijuanaNews.com archives about McCollum with links to others: 

Collectivist Florida Representative McCollum Wins Orwell Award  

For Supporting Government Power; Plans Run For Senate.  

The Fort Myers News-Press owes its readers an apology and an investigation of the states AG.) 

  

 

New potent marijuana no joke 

November 20, 2007 

From Ft.Myers News-Press 

 

Statistics show marijuana is the most popular illegal drug in America, with more than half of our young adults between the ages of 19-28 saying they have used it. But today's marijuana is no Woodstock rerun; it's potent and dangerous. 

 

In the 1960s and '70's, the average THC content (THC produces the high and causes physiological problems) in marijuana was approximately 4 percent. 

(MarijuanaNews note: First, there is no data on marijuana potency from the 1960s.  

 

Second, there is no evidence that more potent cannabis is more dangerous. There is no record of anyone fatally overdosing on marijuana.
See
No, Cannabis Will Not Be The 21st Century Aspirin Because It Doesnt Kill Anyone! People Suffer And Die, While Scientists Try To Pharmaceuticalize The Aspirin Of the 21st Century B.C.  

 

Third, THC, sold as Marinol, is actually an FDA approved drug, and there is no record of it causing any physiological problems.

See
Boasts Roxanne On Its New Marinol.com Web Site.
Doesnt That Mean That It Should Never Have Been Schedule 2 Anyway? 

 

Fourth, after decades of prohibitionist propaganda about the new potent pot, there really seems to have been roughly a doubling of average THC levels, but this does not support McCollums misuse of the data. 

 

As I wrote in 1998 inMarijuana Prohibition And Potency, Price, And Safety --  

"Is Marijuana Stronger Now Than It Was Back In the '60s,  

When Everyone Thought It Was Harmless?": 

In their bookMarijuana Myths; Marijuana Facts,Zimmer and Morgan devote a short chapter to the data on marijuana potency. I recommend this book for many reasons, but this chapter alone is worth the price of the book.  

In it they point out that 1973 a private company PharmChem tested four times as many samples as the government, and the average potency was 1.62%. Did marijuana increase in potency tenfold in one year?
 

Also consider that one sample tested by PharmChem in 1975 was actually 14% THC, which was 20 times the average for the samples tested by the government that year.  

Subsequently, private testing was prohibited, and for 20 years the only data has come from the government, but in 1980 the average potency from government testing was around 2% and has generally varied between 2 and 3% ever since. 


In short, there is no data from the 60s, and data from the 70s does not support the notion that there was only low THC marijuana available. )

(MarijuanaNews note: First, there is no data on marijuana potency from the 1960s.  

 

The THC level in the hydroponic marijuana grown today in Florida has tested up to 30 percent, and the level continues to rise through plant cloning by growers.  

(MarijuanaNews note: First, McCollums statement really proves nothing except that he is innumerate and knows noting about biology. As noted above, there is nothing new about potent pot, but he is comparing an average with an extreme. 

 

In other words, one cannot compare the American average income in 1970 with the 2007 income of a basketball star today and know anything about todays average income. 

 

Second, cloning will not increase THC levels. The whole purpose of cloning is simply to reproduce the characteristics of the original plant. Only selective breeding will change the characteristics of a plant.  

 

Of course, all this sounds so scientific, and that is probably the reason that prohibitionist propaganda talks so much about hydroponics. I will wager that almost all of the grow-ops they have busted were soil based. Hydroponic growing is too difficult and too risky for most growers. I call it hydrophonic because it sounds sinister.)

This increase in potency has not only increased the dangerous physical effects of the drug, but also the addictive nature of marijuana use. Experts believe that the rate of addiction among daily marijuana users is now higher than that among daily alcohol drinkers. 

MarijuanaNews: Experts believe??? The risks of alcohol use are vastly greater than the risks in using marijuana. Alcohol withdrawal can actually be fatal.) 

See 

Walters Tells a New Lie. Oh Happy Day! People Need Treatment If They Are Sent to Treatment, By Definition. And How Do They Treat Marijuana Addicts? We Couldnt Make This Up, But They Did

Hydroponic marijuana in some areas actually trades ounce for ounce with cocaine.  

(MarijuanaNews note: Recycling garbage is a good thing, but I am not so sure about recycling the garbage of prohibitionist propaganda. This line about cannabis being traded for equal amounts of cocaine was originally used for BC Bud which was also supposed to be super potent. 

See 
How the Canadian Prohibitionists Equate Marijuana And Cocaine In the New Party Line

It was never true, as both the RCMP and the DEA made clear.  

It also contradicts the latest claims from the Drug Czar saying that cocaine prices are going up and marijuana prices going down:
From January through June 2007, the mid-level wholesale (involving amounts between one and ten ounces) price per pure gram of cocaine increased 33 per cent, from $53.09 to $70.39.

That would mean that cannabis would be selling for $1,400 an ounce or more, which is absurd. There is no evidence of that. 

The rest of the column is devoted to grow houses. As it happens, todays Orange County Register had an editorial on the subject, which describes the real problem thusly: So the drug warriors don't reduce availability, but they push growers into your neighborhood and increase their profitability. Is that what the drug war was intended to do?)  

(MarijuanaNews note: Recycling garbage is a good thing, but I am not so sure about recycling the garbage of prohibitionist propaganda. This line about cannabis being traded for equal amounts of cocaine was originally used for BC Bud which was also supposed to be super potent. 

The drug is so lucrative that grow houses are popping up in some of the most affluent neighborhoods. These "Marijuana McMansions" are home to multimillion-dollar growing operations. Florida had the second highest number of grow-house seizures in the country in 2006.  

 

One such operation was recently discovered and shut down in North Florida, where an organized ring had been using seven houses to grow and distribute large quantities of marijuana. These grow houses produced 100 pounds of marijuana per month, and traffickers were netting profits of nearly half a million dollars a year. The Attorney General's Office of Statewide Prosecution is prosecuting this case and working with law enforcement to pursue other operations throughout the state. 

 

Grow houses are often the targets of other violent crimes, including home invasions and robberies carried out by rival criminal groups, as the plants alone are worth tens of thousands of dollars. Marijuana is no longer grown and traded by amateurs it is being trafficked by organized and dangerous rings of criminals.  

 

Taking this threat seriously, our state must pass tougher laws to crack down on these sophisticated growing operations. I am supporting legislation sponsored by state Sen. Steve Oelrich, R-Gainesville, and state Rep. Nick Thompson, R-Fort Myers, that lowers from 300 plants to 25 plants the standard for creating a presumption that a person is intending to distribute for profit. 

See
Abuse In Prisons: Iraqi and American. Bush says, That is not the way we do things in America. No, That Is Exactly The Way We Do Things in America! Especially In Texas and Florida.

The bill also creates a new penalty for growers who own a house for the purpose of cultivating marijuana, as well as a new penalty for people who live in or are the caretakers of marijuana grow houses. 

 

It is our responsibility to not only educate our residents, especially those who are younger and may be more susceptible to drug use, about highly potent marijuana, but also to implement new strategies for curbing the spread of this new and dangerous threat. 

--  Bill McCollum is attorney general of Florida.
